definition: A technique that caps the magnitude of gradients during training to prevent instability from exploding gradients.
details: Gradient clipping is especially important when training recurrent networks and large transformers, where occasional large gradients can otherwise destabilize optimization.
story: Imagine teaching a friend to shoot a basketball. They miss, and you walk them backwards through the shot — elbow, wrist, release — to find what needs fixing. It is the same loop you use to learn anything: try, miss, correct, try again. Underneath all the magic is a patient process of small improvements. It is learning from every miss instead of repeating the same mistake. That steady, miss-by-miss improvement is Gradient Clipping.
